questions.question: What is opportunity cost?
choices: The value of the best alternative given up
The total value of every rejected alternative
Only the cash price of a purchase
The value of the option chosen

questions.question: What is a trade-off?
choices: Receiving unlimited resources without sacrifice
A payment collected only by banks
Giving up something to obtain something else
A cost incurred only in foreign trade

questions.question: Which resource creates opportunity costs even when no money is spent?
choices: Price labels
Time
A receipt number
A store's logo

questions.question: What is an explicit cost?
choices: A forgone alternative without payment
A benefit gained from specialization
A past cost that can be recovered
A direct monetary payment

questions.question: What is an implicit cost?
choices: The value of a resource's forgone alternative use
Only a payment shown on an invoice
A price that every seller must charge
A tax imposed on imports

questions.question: What is marginal cost?
choices: The total cost of every previous action
The revenue from all units sold
The additional cost of an extra unit or action
The average benefit of past choices

questions.question: What is a sunk cost?
choices: A cost that changes with the next decision
A cost already incurred that cannot be recovered
A resource available without alternatives
An expected future benefit

questions.question: Why can free admission to an event still involve an opportunity cost?
choices: A zero ticket price means there is no trade-off
Only the organizer can face costs
Time has economic value only when tickets are sold
Attending uses time that could be spent elsewhere

questions.question: Why is opportunity cost not the sum of every rejected choice?
choices: Mutually exclusive alternatives cannot all be chosen instead
Only paid activities have value
All alternatives always have identical benefits
A choice has no value until money changes hands

questions.question: Why should a business consider the owner's forgone salary?
choices: The salary is automatically paid by customers
Only employee wages count as resource costs
The owner could use labor in another job
Forgone income is always a sunk cost

questions.question: How can a wage increase affect the opportunity cost of leisure?
choices: Leisure becomes impossible to choose
An hour of leisure may involve more forgone earnings
The cost of every consumer good must fall
Past work hours become recoverable

questions.question: Why do production possibilities curves show opportunity costs?
choices: Every point guarantees the same level of consumer satisfaction
Only monetary prices determine the curve
The curve measures unemployment without showing output
More of one output can require giving up another

questions.question: What usually happens to opportunity cost when a resource's best alternative becomes more valuable?
choices: It increases
It necessarily becomes zero
It becomes a sunk cost
It disappears from future decisions

questions.question: Why should an unrecoverable past payment generally not determine whether to continue an activity?
choices: Past payments always increase future benefits
Refunds are guaranteed for any discontinued activity
The current decision depends on future benefits and costs
Future alternatives have no economic value

questions.question: Why might two people face different opportunity costs for the same activity?
choices: Opportunity cost is fixed by national law
They have different alternatives and preferences
Only the activity's sticker price matters
Everyone has identical uses for time

questions.question: A student chooses a concert over a work shift that would pay $60. What is the forgone monetary alternative?
choices: The cost of every concert that year
The student's total annual earnings
The wages of everyone at the concert
The $60 in wages

questions.question: A town uses land for a park instead of its next-best option, housing. What is part of the park's opportunity cost?
choices: The benefits of the forgone housing
The benefits of every possible land use combined
Only money already spent on unrelated roads
Only the park's future maintenance bill

questions.question: A factory can make 100 chairs or 50 tables with the same resources. What is the opportunity cost of one table under a constant trade-off?
choices: Half a chair
Fifty chairs
Two chairs
One hundred chairs

questions.question: A nonrefundable ticket has been purchased. Which factor should guide whether to attend now?
choices: The need to recover the ticket through attendance
The expected benefits and additional costs of attending
The ticket price alone regardless of alternatives
The rule that a paid ticket must always be used

questions.question: Which comparison is correct?
choices: Opportunity cost applies only to businesses
Sunk costs are always the best forgone alternative
A free good can never require giving up time
A cash payment and forgone time can both be relevant costs
